lessons.title: Why cracking teaches defense
lessons.body: Cracking your own test hashes is the fastest way to internalise why slow salted hashing matters. Fast unsalted hashes (MD5, raw SHA-256) fall in seconds; bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2 with a good cost factor resist even GPUs. You learn the defense by feeling the attack.

tools.name: Hashcat
tools.what: The leading GPU password cracker. Takes a hash type and a wordlist or mask and tries candidates at enormous speed. Great for proving to yourself how weak fast hashes are.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.install: `sudo apt install hashcat`; a GPU helps but CPU works for learning.
try: hashcat -m 0 -a 0 your_md5_hashes.txt rockyou.txt    # hashes YOU generated
tools.exercise: Hash a list of weak passwords you make up with MD5, crack them with hashcat, then re-hash the same list with bcrypt and try again. Time both. That contrast is the lesson.

tools.name: John the Ripper
tools.what: The classic, format-rich cracker (jumbo edition handles hundreds of hash types). Its *2john helpers turn files (zip, pdf, shadow) into crackable hashes - useful for understanding where hashes hide.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.install: `sudo apt install john` (get the 'jumbo' build for more formats).
try: unshadow /etc/passwd /etc/shadow > mine.txt   # on your OWN machine
tools.exercise: On a throwaway VM you control, add a user with a weak password and crack it from the shadow file. Then set a strong passphrase and watch the wordlist attack fail.
